links.outcome: Accuracy after retina specialist overread of AI-positive results before referral
links.effect: AI alone: sensitivity 95.5%, specificity 60.3%, PPV 47.7%; with specialist overread of MTMDR-positive results: PPV 95.5%, accuracy 97.4%, sensitivity 95.5%, specificity 98.2%. Overread of AI-ungradable raised gradability from 63.5% to 95.6%.
links.quote: Under this 2-step workflow, the positive predictive value increased to 95.5% (95% CI, 86.7%–100%), along with accuracy of 97.4%, sensitivity of 95.5% (95% CI, 86.7%–100%), and specificity of 98.2% (95% CI, 94.6%–100%) ( Figs 6 , 15 ).

links.outcome: Real-world local performance and gradability of autonomous AI in nonmydriatic primary care
links.effect: Accuracy 70.0%, sensitivity 95.5%, specificity 60.3% vs in-person exam; gradability 62.5% vs 93.1% for retina specialists, unlike balanced pivotal-trial performance.
links.quote: The comparison of the AI system to in-person examination had a 70.0% accuracy including 95.5% sensitivity (95% CI, 86.7%–100%) and 60.3% specificity (95% CI, 47.7%–72.9%) ( Figs 5 , 6 , S7 , S8 ).

links.outcome: AI discrepancy rates by age, sex, and race/ethnicity
links.effect: No significant association of discrepancies with age (P = 0.74), sex (P = 0.061), or White vs non-White race (P = 0.50); N = 1222.
links.quote: Artificial intelligence performance did not differ across age, sex, or self-reported race or ethnicity.

openai.sample_unit: patient screening encounters (790 human-only phase; 1222 AI phase)

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance after specialist verification of AI-positive screening results
links.effect: Simulated specialist overread increased positive predictive value from 47.7% to 95.5%, specificity from 60.3% to 98.2%, and accuracy from 70.0% to 97.4%; sensitivity remained 95.5%.
links.quote: Under this 2-step workflow, the positive predictive value increased to 95.5% (95% CI, 86.7%–100%), along with accuracy of 97.4%, sensitivity of 95.5% (95% CI, 86.7%–100%), and specificity of 98.2% (95% CI, 94.6%–100%) ( Figs 6 , 15 ).

links.outcome: Interpretability of AI-ungradable screening encounters after human fallback
links.effect: A single specialist interpreted 88.1% of AI-ungradable encounters; adjudicated consensus found 77.7% interpretable. AI alone returned ungradable results in 36.5% of encounters.
links.quote: A single experienced retina specialist was able to interpret 93.1% of all patient encounters as well as 88.1% of AI-ungradable encounters, and an adjudicated consensus agreed that the image was interpretable in 77.7% of cases.

links.outcome: Associations between diagnostic discrepancies and demographic subgroups
links.effect: No statistically significant associations: age P = 0.74; sex P = 0.061; White vs. non-White race P = 0.50; N = 1222.
links.quote: Encounters in which there was a discrepancy in the DR diagnosis between the AI system and the in-person examination result did not show any statistically significant predilection for age, sex, or self-reported race or ethnicity (Student’s 2-tailed t test for age, P = 0.74; chi-square statistic for sex, 3.51, P = 0.061; chi-square statistic for White vs. non-White race, 0.446, P = 0.50; N = 1222).

links.effect: A hybrid AI-human workflow achieved 95.5% sensitivity and 98.2% specificity, compared to 60.3% specificity for AI alone.
links.quote: A 2-step AI-human hybrid workflow in which the AI algorithm initially rendered an assessment followed by overread by a retina specialist of MTMDR-positive encounters resulted in a sensitivity of 95.5% (95% CI, 86.7%-100%) and a specificity of 98.2% (95% CI, 94.6%-100%).
